semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {عَمَّا قَلِيلٍ}: There are two views on this «ما». The first: it is redundant (zāʾida), inserted between the preposition and its genitive noun for emphasis, just as it is inserted after the «باء», as in {فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ} [Āl ʿImrān: 159], and after «مِنْ», as in {مِّمَّا خطيائاتهم} [Nūḥ: 25]. And «قليلٍ» is an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted noun of time, i.e. «عَنْ زمنٍ قليل» ("after a short time").
The second: it is not redundant but an indefinite noun meaning "a thing" or "a time", and «قليل» is its adjective or a substitute (badal) for it. As for this preposition and its genitive noun, there are three views. The first: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying {لَّيُصْبِحُنَّ}, i.e. "they will surely become, after a short time, regretful." The second: it is attached to «نادمين». This depends on one of the opinions concerning the oath-lām, of which there are three: first, that it is permissible to place before it what is governed by what follows it, without restriction; this is the view of al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayda. Second: that this is prohibited without restriction; this is the view of the majority of the Basrans. Third: a distinction between the adverbial (ẓarf) and its equivalent on the one hand and other things on the other: latitude is permitted in the former and forbidden in the latter, so it is not permissible to say «زيداً لأضرِبَنَّ» for «والله لأضربنَّ زيداً», because «زيداً» is neither an adverbial nor its equivalent.
The third of the views mentioned above: it is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «عَمَّا قليلٍ نُنْصَرُ» ("after a short time we shall be given victory"), omitted because what precedes it indicates it, namely His saying {رَبِّ انْصُرْني}.
It has also been read «لَتُصْبِحُنَّ» with the tā᾽ of address, either as a shift of person (iltifāt), or on the basis that the statement was made by the Messenger to his people.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {غُثَآءً}: the second object of «جَعْل» in the sense of "making into". As for «الغُثاء»: it is said to be the «جُفاء» (scum, foam-rubbish), which has already been discussed in [Sūrat] al-Raʿd; this is al-Akhfash's statement. Al-Zajjāj said: "It is the withered part of the leaves of trees, which, when the flood runs, mixes with its foam." It is also said: it is everything that the flood and the cooking-pot throw up of what is of no use, and the proverb is made with it in that sense. Its final radical is a wāw, since it is from «غثا الوادي يَغْثُو غَثْوَاً», and likewise «غَثَت القِدْرُ». As for «غَثِيَتْ نفسُه تَغْثِي غَثَياناً», meaning "it became foul", it is close in meaning but belongs to the root with yāʾ. The thāʾ of «الغُثَّاء» may be doubled or lightened, and it has been pluralised as «أَغْثاء», which is irregular (shādhdh); the regular form would have been «أَغْثِيَة» like «أَغْرِبة», or «غِثْيان» like «غِرْبان» and «غِلْمان». They recited a verse of Imruʾ al-Qays:
3417 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... من السَّيْلِ والغُثَّاءِ فَلْكَةُ مُغْزَلِ
(". . . of the flood and the debris, a spindle-whorl"), with the thāʾ both doubled and lightened, and the plural, i.e. «والأَغْثاء».
His saying: {فَبُعْداً لِّلْقَوْمِ}: «بُعْداً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that stands in place of the utterance of its verb, so the verb that governs it must be omitted, because it has the meaning of a supplication against them. The original is «بَعُدَ بُعْدَاً وبَعَداً» like «رَشَدَ رُشْداً ورَشَداً». There are two views about this lām. The first, which is the apparent one: it is attached to an omitted element, for clarification (li-l-bayān), like the lām in «سَقْياً له» and «جَدْعاً له»; this is al-Zamakhsharī's view. The second: it is attached to «بُعْداً»; this is the view of al-Ḥawfī. This is rejected, because the omission of this lām together with the maṣdar's reaching its genitive noun is not attested at all. For that reason they prohibited the ishtighāl construction in His saying {والذين كَفَرُواْ فَتَعْساً لَّهُمْ} [Muḥammad: 8], since the lām is not attached to «تَعْساً» but to an omitted element, even though al-Zamakhsharī permitted that; it will come in its place, if Allah the Exalted wills.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {تَتْرَى}: there are two views on it. The first, which is the apparent one: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رُسُلَنا», in the sense of "successive", i.e. one after another, or "consecutive", according to the disagreement about its meaning, as will come. In reality it is a maṣdar standing in the place of the ḥāl. The second: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being «إرسالاً تَتْرى», i.e. "consecutively", or "sending after sending".
Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it «تَتْرَىً» with tanwīn, and this is also the reading of al-Shāfiʿī. The rest of the Seven read «تترى» with a plain alif and no tanwīn, and this is the well-known dialect. Whoever gives it tanwīn has several views. The first: that the pattern of the word is faʿl, like «فَلْس», so «تَتْرَىً» is like your saying «نَصَرْتُه نَصْراً»; its pattern in their reading is «فَعْلاً». This view has been rejected on the ground that it is not attested that the case-endings run over its rā᾽, so that one would say «هذا تَتْرٌ ومررت بتَتْرٍ», like «هذا نَصْرٌ، ورأيت نصراً، ومررتُ بنصرٍ». Since that is not attested, it is invalid for its pattern to be faʿl. The second: that its alif is for ilḥāq (extension to match a quadriliteral pattern) with «جَعْفر», like the alif in «أَرْطى» and «عَلْقى»; when it takes tanwīn the alif is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. This is closer than the previous view, but it implies the existence of an ilḥāq alif in verbal nouns, which is rare. The third: that it is a feminine-marking alif like «دعوى», and this is clear. So there are three views about its alif: first, that it is a replacement for the tanwīn in pause; second, that it is for ilḥāq; third, that it is for feminine marking. There is also disagreement over whether it is a maṣdar like «دعوى» and «ذكرى», or a collective noun (ism jamʿ) like «أسرى» and «شتى»; thus Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] stated both. There is something to consider in this, since the well-known view is that «أسرى» and «شَتَّى» are broken plurals, not collective nouns. Its first radical is originally a wāw, because it is from «المُواترة» and «الوِتْر», and it was changed into tāʾ, just as it was changed into tāʾ in «تَوْارة», «تَوْلج», «تَيْقُور», «تُخَمَة», «تُراث» and «تُجاه», which are from «الوَرْي», «الوُلوج», «الوَقار», «الوَخامة», «الوِراثة» and «الوَجْه».
They disagreed about its meaning. From al-Aṣmaʿī: one after another, with an interval between them. Others said: it is from «المُواترة», which is succession without an interval. Al-Rāghib said: "«التواتُرُ» is the succession of a thing one by one, singly. The Exalted said: {ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا تَتْرَى}. «والوَتِيْرَة» is disposition and way; it is said: 'they are on one watīra.' «والتِرَةُ» is vengeance. «والوَتيرة» is the partition between the two nostrils."
His saying: {أَحَادِيثَ}: it is said to be a plural of «حديث», but an irregular one. It is also said: rather, it is a plural of «أُحْدُوْثَة», like «أُضْحُوكة». Al-Akhfash said: "This is said only of evil, not of good. The Arabs deviated in a few words and pluralised them on the pattern «مَفاعيل», such as «أَباطيل» and «أَقاطيع»." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الأحاديث» may be a collective noun for «الحديث», and from it comes «أحاديث رسول الله ﷺ»." Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "«أَفاعيل» is not among the patterns of collective nouns; our colleagues mentioned it only among irregular plurals, like «قَطيع» and «أقاطيع». And if «عَباديد» has been judged a broken plural although no singular of it has been uttered, then all the more so «أحاديث», for which a singular has been uttered, namely «حديث». So it is clear that it is a broken plural, not a collective noun, for the reason we have mentioned."

semin-durr:45-45.t: His saying: {هَارُونَ}: it may be a badal (substitute), or a bayān (explicative apposition), or accusative by the implied verb «أَعْني» ("I mean").

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying: {لِبَشَرَيْنِ}: «بَشَر» applies to the singular, the dual and the plural, the masculine and the feminine. The Exalted said: {مَآ أَنتُمْ إِلاَّ بَشَرٌ}. Sometimes it agrees [in number], and this verse is an instance. As for the singular form of «مِثْلِنا», it is because it behaves like the maṣdars in being singular and masculine, and it is never made feminine at all; sometimes it agrees with what it describes in the dual, as in His saying {مِّثْلَيْهِمْ رَأْيَ العين} [Āl ʿImrān: 13], and in the plural, as in His saying {ثُمَّ لاَ يكونوا أَمْثَالَكُم} [Muḥammad: 38]. It is also said: likeness in humanity is meant, not in quantity. And it is said: the singular suffices in place of the dual.
His saying: {وَقَوْمُهُمَا لَنَا عَابِدُونَ}: a ḥāl clause.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا موسى الكتاب}: it is said that He meant the people of Moses, so the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place; for that reason He repeated the pronoun in «لعلَّهم» referring to them. There is something to consider in this, since the pronoun may return to the people without assuming their annexation to Moses, their guidance then being dependent on the giving of the Torah to Moses.

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {وَمَعِينٍ}: an adjective of an omitted described noun, i.e. «وماءٍ مَعِيْنٍ» ("and flowing water"). There are two views on it. The first: that its mīm is redundant, and its origin is «مَعْيُوْن», i.e. "seen by the eye", and it underwent the same weakening as «مبيع» and its type; it is like their saying «كَبَدْتُه», i.e. "I struck his liver", and «رَأَسْتُه», i.e. "I hit his head", and «عِنْته», i.e. "I perceived him with my eye". For that reason al-Khalīl placed it under the root ع ي ن. The second: that the mīm is original, and its pattern is faʿīl, derived from «المَعْن». There is disagreement about «المَعْن»: it is said to be the small amount, and from it comes «الماعُون». And it is said: it is from «مَعَنَ الشيءُ مَعانَةً», i.e. "the thing became abundant". Jarīr said:
3418 - إنَّ الذين غَدَوْا بِلُبِّك غادَروا ... وَشَلاً بعينِك لا يَزال مَعيناً
("Those who went off with your reason left a trickle in your eye that never ceases to flow.")
Al-Rāghib said: "It is from «مَعَن الماءُ»: the water flowed," and he called the courses of water «مُعْنان». "«وأمعنَ الفرس»: the horse went far in its running; «وأَمْعَنَ بحقي»: he went off with my right; and «فلان مَعَنٌ في حاجته»", meaning quick. I say: all of it goes back to the meaning of flowing and speed.

semin-durr:51-51.t: His saying: {واعملوا صَالِحاً}: «صالحاً» may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. «واعملوا عَمَلاً صالحاً» ("do righteous work"), without regard to what they do, as in their saying «تُعْطي وتمْنع» ("you give and you withhold"). And it may be a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), applying to the very thing that is done.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {وَإِنَّ هذه أُمَّتُكُمْ}: Ibn ʿĀmir alone read «وأنْ» هذه with fatḥa on the hamza and a lightened nūn. The Kufans read it with kasra and a doubled nūn, and the rest with fatḥa and a doubled nūn. As for Ibn ʿĀmir's reading, it is the lightened form of the heavy «أنَّ»; the explanation of the fatḥa in the heavy form will come, and the meaning of his reading will then be clear. As for the Kufans' reading, it is on the basis of resumption (istiʾnāf).
As for the reading of the rest, there are three views on it. The first: that it is on the omission of the lām, i.e. «ولأَِنَّ هذه»; when the particle was omitted, the well-known disagreement [about the status of the noun after the omitted preposition] arose. This lām is attached to «اتَّقون». The discussion of the fāʾ is like the discussion of His saying {وَإِيَّايَ فارهبون} [al-Baqara: 40]. The second: that it is conjoined to «بما تَعْملون», i.e. "I am aware of what you do and of the fact that this ..."; so «هذه» falls within the scope of what is known. The third: that there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being «واعلموا أنَّ هذه أمَّتُكم» ("and know that this is your community").

semin-durr:53-53.t: It has already been discussed — {فتقطعوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ زُبُراً} — together with what was said about the two [words] and what was read in them, so there is no need to repeat it.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
Their saying: {فِي غَمْرَتِهِمْ}: the second object of «ذَرْهم», i.e. "leave them settled in their ghamra". It may also be an adverbial of the leaving, the second object being omitted. «الغَمْرَةُ» in origin is the water that covers a man's stature, and «الغَمْرُ» is the water that covers the earth; then that was borrowed for ignorance, so it is said "so-and-so is in a ghamra". The root denotes covering and concealment; from it comes «الغُمْرُ» with ḍamma for one who has not tried affairs, and «غُِمارُ الناسِ» and «خُمَارُهم» meaning their throng. «والغِمْر» with kasra is rancour, because it covers the heart. «والغَمَرات» are hardships. «والغامِرُ» is one who throws himself into perils. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«والغَمْرَةُ» is the water that covers a man's stature; it was used as a parable for them, for the ignorance and blindness in which they are [submerged]. Or they were likened to those playing in a deep pool of water, because of the falsehood they are upon, as in the verse:
3419 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كأنني ضاربٌ في غَمْرَةٍ لَعِبُ
("as if I were one striking about in a deep pool, playing")."
The Commander of the Faithful, Abū Ḥaywa and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «غَمَراتهم» in the plural, because each of them has a ghamra of his own. The reading of the majority does not reject this meaning, since it is a generic noun in annexation.

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying: {أَنَّمَا نُمِدُّهُمْ}: there are three views on this «ما». The first: it means «الذي» (that which) and is the noun of «أنْ», with «نُمِدُّهم» its ṣila (relative clause) and its returning pronoun (ʿāʾid). «ومن مال» is a ḥāl from the relative noun, or an explication of it, and is attached to an omitted element. «ونُسارعُ» is the khabar of «أنَّ». The returning pronoun from this clause to the noun of «أنَّ» is omitted, its implied form being «نُسارِعُ لهم به» or «فيه», except that omitting the like of this is rare. It is also said: the link between this clause and the noun of «أنَّ» is the overt noun that stands in place of the pronoun, namely «في الخيرات», since the original is «نُسارِعُ لهم فيه», and He placed «الخيرات» in its place for glorification and to draw attention to its being among the good things. This proceeds according to the school of al-Akhfash, who holds that linkage may be by overt nouns even if they are not the same word as the first, so he permits «زيد الذي قام أبو عبد الله» when «أبو عبد الله» is the kunya of Zayd. Examples of this from him have preceded. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is not permissible for the khabar to be «مِنْ مالٍ», because it was «مِنْ مال», and they are not reproached for that; rather they are reproached for their belief that those possessions are good for them."
The second: that «ما» is maṣdarī (verbal-noun-forming), so a maṣdar is formed from it and what follows it, which is the noun of «أنَّ», and «نُسارع» is the khabar. On this it is necessary to omit the maṣdarī «أنْ» before «نُسارع» for the predication to be sound, the implied form being «أَنْ نسارعَ»; when «أنْ» was omitted, the imperfect after it became nominative. The sense is: "Do they think that our supplying them with such-and-such is a hastening on our part to give them good things?" The third: that it is a preparing, restraining particle (muhayyiʾa kāffa). Al-Kisāʾī said this about this verse, and in that case one pauses at «وَبَنِين», because after the verb of thinking there has come about a relation of predicate and subject, as in «حَسِبْتُ أنَّما ينطلق عمروٌ» and «أنما تقومُ أنت».
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read «إنما» with kasra on the hamza, as resumption, in which case the two objects of «الحُسْبان» are omitted, by restriction or abbreviation. Ibn Kathīr in one transmission read «يُمِدُّهم» with yāʾ, the subject being Allah the Exalted. By analogy he would read «يُسارع» with yāʾ as well. Al-Sulamī and Ibn Abī Bakra read «يُسارع» with yāʾ and kasra on the rā᾽. Its subject has two views: first, the Creator the Exalted; second, the pronoun of the relative «ما», if we take it as meaning «الذي», or the maṣdar if we take it as maṣdarī. In that case «يسارِعُ لهم» is the khabar. On the first one needs to imply a returning pronoun, i.e. «يُسارع اللهُ لهم به» or «فيه»; on the second there is no need, since the subject is the pronoun of the relative «ما».
Also from the aforementioned Abū Bakra: «يُسارَع» with yāʾ, in the passive, «في الخيرات» being the deputy agent; the clause is the khabar of «أنَّ» and the returning pronoun is omitted as previously. Al-Ḥasan read «نُسْرع» with nūn, from «أَسْرَعَ», and it is like «نُسارع» in what was said above.
And {بَل لاَّ يَشْعُرُونَ} is an iḍrāb (turning away) from the thinking that was asked about with a question of rebuke, and it is an iḍrāb of transition.

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {مِّنْ خَشْيةِ رَبِّهِمْ}: there are two views on it. The first: that it is for stating the kind (bayān al-jins). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is for stating the kind of apprehension." I say: that is an awkward expression. The second: that it is attached to «مُشْفِقُون»; al-Ḥawfī said this, and it is clear.

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying: {يُؤْتُونَ مَآ آتَواْ}: the majority hold that it is from «الإِتياء» (giving), i.e. "they give what they gave". ʿĀʾisha, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash read «يَأْتُون ما أَتَواْ», from «الإِتيان» (doing), i.e. "they do what they did of acts of obedience". Abū l-Baqāʾ confined his mention of the disagreement to «أتَوْا» with the short alif only. That is not good, because it suggests that whoever read «أَتَوْا» with the short alif read «يُؤْتُون» from the quadriliteral verb; but that is not so.
His saying: {وَّقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ}: this clause is a ḥāl from the agent of «يُؤْتُوْن», so the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl.
His saying «أنَّهم»: the implied form may be «وَجِلةُ مِنْ أنَّهم», i.e. "fearful of their return to their Lord"; or it may be «لأنَّهم», i.e. the cause of the fear is the return to their Lord.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {أولئك يُسَارِعُونَ}: this clause is the khabar of «إنَّ الذين». Al-Aʿmash read «إنهم» with kasra, as resumption, so pausing at «وَجِلة» is complete or sufficient. Al-Ḥurr read «يُسْرِعُون», from «أَسْرع». Al-Zajjāj said: "«يُسارِعُون» is more emphatic," meaning that the form mufāʿala indicates strength of the action because of the contest involved.
His saying: {وَهُمْ لَهَا سَابِقُونَ}: there are several views about the pronoun in «لها». The most apparent: that it refers to «الخيرات» because it was mentioned earlier in the wording. It is also said: it refers to Paradise. And: to happiness. And: to the nations. The apparent view is that «سابقون» is the khabar, and «لها» is attached to it, put first for the sake of the verse-ending and for specification. The lām is said to mean «إلى»; one says «سَبَقْتُ له» and «سَبَقْتُ إليه» with one meaning. The object of «سابقون» is omitted, its implied form being «سابقون الناسَ إليها» ("outstripping people to them"). It is also said that the lām is causal, i.e. "outstripping people for their sake". This clause is then an emphasis of the clause before it, namely «يُسارِعُون في الخيرات», and it conveys a further meaning, namely permanence and stability, after the first indicated renewal.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. 'doers of the outstripping for its sake', or 'outstripping people for its sake'." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "In my view these two statements are one." I say: they are not one, for by the first implied reading he means that no object is implied for the outstripping at all; the aim is only to inform that outstripping occurs from them, without regard to whom they outstripped, as in His sayings {يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ} [al-Baqara: 258] and {وَكُلُواْ واشربوا} [al-Baqara: 187], and "he gives and withholds". His aim in the second reading is to imply an object that was omitted because of the indication [of context], and the lām is causal in both readings.
Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "Or 'they are outstripping it', i.e. they attain it before the Hereafter, since it was hastened for them in this world." I say: he means that «لها» is the object of «سابقون», the lām having been added to the object. Two things make its addition good, each of which would, if it stood alone, imply permissibility: that the governing word is derivative, and that its governed element is placed before it. The Shaykh said: "The wording «لها سابِقُون» does not indicate this interpretation, because one thing's outstripping another indicates the precedence of the outstripper over the outstripped; so how can He say: 'and they outstrip the good things'? This is not sound." I say: I do not know from what angle it is unsound. It is as if he imagined that the outstripper precedes the outstripped, so how can they meet? But he should have said: "how can He say: 'and they attain the good things', when they do not meet them because they have gone ahead of them?" — unless the pen slipped ahead of him and he wrote «وهم يَسْبِقون» in place of «وهم يَنالون». In any case, where is the unsoundness?
Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "It is possible that «وهم لها سابقون» is a khabar after a khabar, and the meaning of «وهم لها» is like the meaning of the verse:
3420 - أنت لها أحمدُ مِنْ بينِ البَشَرْ ...
("You, for it, O Aḥmad, from among mankind ..."),
meaning that this description with which He described the righteous does not go beyond the limit of capacity and ability." So there are three views about the lām: first, that it means «إلى»; second, that it is causal in its normal sense; third, that it is redundant. And on the khabar of the mubtadaʾ there are two views: first, that it is «سابِقون», which is the apparent one; second, that it is the preposition and its genitive noun, as in the verse:
أنت لها أحمدُ مِنْ بينِ البَشَرْ ...
Al-Ṭabarī preferred it, and it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.

semin-durr:62-62.t: His saying: {يَنطِقُ}: an adjective of «كِتاب». And «بالحق» may be attached to «يَنْطِقُ», or attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from its agent, i.e. "speaks, accompanied by the truth".

semin-durr:63-63.t: His saying: {هُمْ لَهَا عَامِلُونَ}: like His saying {هُمْ لَهَا سَابِقُونَ}.

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His saying: {حتى إِذَآ}: this «حتى» is either a particle of commencement (ḥarf ibtidāʾ), the conditional clause after it being a limit for what precedes it, with the second «إذا» being the «إذا» of suddenness (fujāʾiyya) that is the apodosis of the conditional; or, according to some, a preposition. Its investigation has been given more than once. Al-Ḥawfī said: "«حتى» is [a particle of] limit, and it is a conjunction; «إذا» is an adverbial annexed to what follows it and contains the sense of condition; the second «إذا» is in the position of the apodosis of the first; the meaning of the speech operates in «إذا», the meaning being 'they cried out'; and the operator in the second is «أَخَذْنا»." This is speech that is not clear.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«حتى» is a particle of commencement and nothing else. «إذا» and the second [«إذا»] which is its apodosis prevent «حتى» from being a limit for «عامِلُون»." I say: he means that the conditional clause and its apodosis cannot apparently be a limit for «عامِلون». The apparent sense of Makkī's words is that it is a limit for «عامِلون», for he said: "i.e. the disbelievers of Quraysh have deeds of evil, other than the deeds of the people of piety, which they are doing, until Allah seizes the people of luxury and arrogance among them, when they cry out." End of quotation.
«والجُؤَار» is shouting in general. Al-Jawharī recited:
3421 - يُراوِحُ مِنْ صَلَواتِ المَلِيْ ... كِ طَوْراً سُجوداً وطَوْراً جُؤارا
("He alternates in the prayers to the King, at times in prostration and at times in loud supplication.")
This has already been treated exhaustively in [Sūrat] al-Naḥl.

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying: {على أَعْقَابِكُمْ}: there are two views on it. The first: that it is attached to «تَنْكِصُون», as in His saying {نَكَصَ على عَقِبَيْهِ} [al-Anfāl: 48]? The second: that it is attached to an omitted element, as it is a ḥāl from the agent of «تَنْكِصُون»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this, and there is no need for it. The Commander of the Faithful read «تَنْكُصُون» with ḍamma on the ʿayn [middle radical]; it is a dialectal form.
[Translator's note: the question mark after the Quranic citation in the first view is in the source as printed.]

semin-durr:67-67.t:
His saying: {مُسْتَكْبِرِينَ}: a ḥāl from the agent of «تَنْكِصُون». His saying «به»: there are two views on it. The first: that it is attached to «مُسْتكْبرين». The second: that it is attached to «سامِراً». On the first, the pronoun refers to the Qur'an, or to the House (may Allah the Exalted honour it), or to the Messenger ﷺ, or to the turning back indicated by «تَنْكِصون», as in His saying {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ} [al-Māʾida: 8]. The bāʾ in all of this is causal, because they were arrogant on account of the Qur'an when it was recited to them, and on account of the House, because they say "we are its custodians", and on account of the Messenger because they say "he is from us, not from others", or on account of the turning back, because it is the cause of the arrogance. It is also said: arrogance was made to include the sense of denial, which is why it is made transitive with the bāʾ; and this works if the pronoun refers to the Qur'an or to the Messenger.
As for the second, which is its attachment to «سامِراً», the pronoun may refer to what it referred to in the foregoing, except the turning back, because they used to spend the night in conversation about the Qur'an and about the Messenger, i.e. they made them their topic of talk, in which they plunged, as one converses at night about tales; and they used to spend the night conversing at the House. So the bāʾ here is locative, and «سامِراً» is accusative as a ḥāl, either from the agent of «تَنْكِصُون» or from the pronoun in «مُسْتَكْبرين».
Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ḥaywa, and it is also related from Abū ʿAmr, read «سُمَّراً» with ḍamma on the fāʾ [first radical] and fatḥa on the ʿayn [middle radical], doubled. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abū Rajāʾ and Ibn ʿAbbās also [read] «سُمَّاراً" likewise, except with an added alif between the mīm and the rā᾽. Both are plurals of «سامِر», and both are regular plurals of the adjectival fāʿil, like «ضُرَّب» and «ضُرَّاب» for «ضارِب». The most eloquent is the singular, because it applies, in singular form, to more than one; you say «قومٌ سامِرٌ» ("a group of night-talkers"). «السَّامِرُ» is taken from «السَّمَر», which is staying awake at night; it is taken from «السَّمَر», which is the moonlight that falls on trees, so they sit by it and converse, finding comfort in it. The poet said:
3422 - كأَن لم يكُنْ بين الحَجونِ إلى الصَّفا ... أنيسٌ ولم يَسْمُرْ بمكةَ سامِرُ
("As if there had been, between al-Ḥajūn and al-Ṣafā, no companion, and no night-talker had ever conversed in Mecca.")
Al-Rāghib said: "«السَّامِرُ» is the dark night; and 'I will not come to you as long as the two sons of Samīr converse', meaning night and day. «والسُّمْرة» is one of the colours, and «السَّمْراء» is used allusively for wheat."
His saying: {تَهْجُرُونَ}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the jīm, and it admits two views. The first: that it is from «الهَجْر» with sukūn on the jīm, which is cutting off and turning away, i.e. "you forsake the verses of Allah and His Messenger and are indifferent to them, so you do not connect with them". The second: that it is from «الهَجَر» with fatḥa, which is raving. One says «هَجَر المريضُ هَجَراً», i.e. he raved, so it has no object. Nāfiʿ and Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the jīm, from «أهجر إهْجاراً», i.e. he spoke obscenely. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "He means reviling the Companions." Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Abū Nuhayk read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ, fatḥa on the hāʾ and a doubled kasra on the jīm, the imperfect of «هَجَّر» with doubling, and it admits being an intensive of «الهَجْر», «الهَجَر» or «الهُجْر». Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim read it like the majority except with a yāʾ (third person), which is a shift of person (iltifāt).

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying: {وَلَوِ اتبع}: the majority read the wāw with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Ibn Waththāb [read it] with ḍamma, by analogy with the pronoun wāw, just as the pronoun wāw is given kasra by analogy with it.
His saying: {بَلْ أَتَيْنَاهُمْ}: the majority attribute the verb to the pronoun of the speaker who magnifies himself; what is meant is "Our messengers came to them." Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read «آتيناهم» with madd, meaning "We gave them"; the second object may then be unmentioned, or it may be «بذِكْرِهم» with the bāʾ redundant in it. Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and also Abū ʿAmr [read] «أَتَيْتُهم» with the tāʾ of the single speaker. Abū l-Barhasam, Abū Ḥaywa, al-Jaḥdarī and Abū Rajāʾ [read] «أَتَيْتُهُمْ» with the tāʾ of the addressee, which is the Messenger, peace be upon him. And ʿĪsā [read] «بذكراهم» with the feminine alif. Qatāda [read] «نُذَكِّرُهم» with the nūn of the speaker who magnifies himself in place of the preposition bāʾ, the imperfect of the intensive «ذَكَّر», and «نُذَكِّرُهم» would be a ḥāl clause. The discussion of «خَرْجاً» and «خَراج» has already been given in [Sūrat] al-Kahf.

semin-durr:74-74.t: His saying: {عَنِ الصراط}: attached to «ناكِبون»; the lām of commencement does not prevent that, according to a view whose investigation has already been given. «النُّكُوب» and «النَّكْب» are turning aside and inclining. From it comes «النَّكْباء», the wind between two winds, so called for its deviating from the usual directions of blowing; and «نَكَبَتْ حوداثُ الدهر» means the misfortunes of time blew like the nakbāʾ. «والمَنْكِبُ» is the meeting-place between the upper arm and the shoulder-blade. «والأَنْكَبُ» is one whose shoulder inclines. And "so-and-so has a nikāba among his people", i.e. a niqāba (office of chief); it seems that the kāf is a replacement for the qāf. One says «نَكَبَ» and «نَكَّب», lightened and doubled.

semin-durr:75-75.t:
His saying: {لَّلَجُّواْ}: the apodosis of «لو». Two lāms occur in succession in it, and this weakens the statement of those who say that when its apodosis is negated with «لم» and the like, in which the negative particle begins with a lām, the entry of the lām is not permitted. If you said «لو قام زيدٌ لَلَمْ يقم عمروٌ», it would not be permissible, he said, so that two lāms should not come together. Yet this occurs in the affirmative, as in this verse, and it was not prevented; otherwise what is the difference between negation and affirmation in that?
«واللَّجاجُ» is persisting in obstinacy in practising the act from which one is forbidden. From it comes «اللَّجَّة» with fatḥa for the repeated sound, as in the verse:
4323 - في لَجَّةٍ أَمْسِكْ فُلاناً عن فُلِ ...
("In an uproar — hold so-and-so back from so-and-so ...")
[Translator's note: the verse number is printed as 4323 in the source; the surrounding verses are numbered in the 3400s, so 3423 may be intended.]
«ولُجَّة البحرِ» is for the repeated movement of its waves. «ولُجَّةُ الليلِ» is for the repeated onset of its darkness. «واللَّجْلَجَةُ» is the repetition of speech, being a reduplication of «لَجَّ». One says «لَجَّ» and «أَلجَّ».

semin-durr:76-76.t: His saying: {فَمَا استكانوا}: «استكان» has already come before it, in [Sūrat] Āl ʿImrān. The first came in the past tense and the second in the imperfect; they did not come as two pasts or two imperfects, nor the first imperfect and the second past. This is because the past conveys the occurrence and realisation of the act, which suits submission (istikāna) better, whereas for supplication (taḍarruʿ) He reports of them the negation of that in the future. As for submission, it may well have occurred from them. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said «وما تَضَرَّعوا فما يَسْتَكِيْنون»? I say: because the meaning is 'We tried them, and no submission was found from them following the trial, and it is not these people's habit to submit and supplicate until the door of severe punishment is opened upon them'." I say: the apparent sense of this is that «حتى» is a limit for the negation of submission and supplication.

semin-durr:77-77.t: «فَتَّحنا» has also been read with doubling. The discussion of «إذا» and «إذا» has already been given recently. Al-Sulamī read «مُبْلَسُوْن» with fatḥa on the lām, from «أَبْلَسه», i.e. he plunged him into despair (iblās).

semin-durr:80-80.t: His saying: {أَفَلاَ تَعْقِلُونَ}: Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read «يَعْقِلون» with the yāʾ of the third person, as a shift of person (iltifāt).

semin-durr:85-85.t: His saying: {سَيَقُولُونَ اللَّهُ}: Abū ʿAmr read «سيقولون اللهُ» in the last two [instances] without the prepositional lām, putting the Majestic Name in the nominative as an answer in keeping with the wording of «مَنْ» in His sayings: «سيقولون اللهُ، قل: أفلا تَتَّقون» and «سيقولون اللهُ، قُلْ فأنى تُسْحَرون», because what is asked about is nominative in position, namely «مَنْ», so its answer came nominative, matching it in wording; and the two places were written so in the Basran codices. The rest [read] «لله» in the two places with the lām, which is an answer according to the meaning, since there is no difference between His saying «مَنْ ربُّ السماوات» and His saying «لِمَنِ السماوات», nor between «مَنْ بيده» and «لِمَنْ له», except for the preposition. This is like your saying: "Who is the owner of this house?", to which one replies "Zayd", or, if you wish, "[It belongs] to Zayd", because in the question there is no difference between saying "To whom does this house belong?" and "Who is its owner?" The lām is written in their codices, so each followed his own codex. There is no disagreement about the first [instance] being «لله», because it is written with the lām; and the answer came with the lām as in the question. Had it been omitted from the answer it would have been permissible, because there is no difference between «لِمَن الأرضُ» and «مَنْ رَبُّ الأرض», except that no one has read it so.

semin-durr:90-90.t: His saying: {بَلْ أَتَيْنَاهُمْ}: some of what was read in its counterpart has been read here too: Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «أَتَيْتَهم» with the tāʾ of the addressee, and others with the tāʾ of the speaker.

semin-durr:91-91.t:
His saying: {إِذاً لَّذَهَبَ}: «إذَنْ» is an answer and a consequence (jawāb wa-jazāʾ). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: «إذَنْ» enters only upon speech that is an answer and a consequence, so how does His saying «لَذَهَبَ» come as an answer and consequence when no condition and no questioner's question has preceded it? I say: the condition is omitted, its implied form being «لو كان معه آلهةٌ» ('if there had been gods with Him'), omitted because of the indication of {وما كان معه مِنْ إلَهٍ}." I say: this is the view of al-Farrāʾ, and it has already been given in [Sūrat] al-Isrāʾ in His saying {وَإِذاً لاَّتَّخَذُوكَ} [verse 73].
His saying: {عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ}: «تَصِفُون» has also been read, with the tāʾ of the addressee. It is a shift of person (iltifāt).

semin-durr:92-92.t:
His saying: {عَالِمِ الغيب}: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read it in the genitive, as a badal from the Majestic Name. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "an adjective of Allah", as if it had become purely a matter of annexation, so the muḍāf became definite. The rest [read] it in the nominative by way of cutting off (qaṭʿ), as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.
His saying: {فتعالى}: a conjunction upon the meaning of what has preceded, as if He had said "He knows the unseen, so He is exalted", like your saying "Zayd is brave, so his rank is great", i.e. he became brave, so he became great. Or it is on the implication of "saying", i.e. "I say: so Allah is exalted".

semin-durr:93-93.t: His saying: {إِمَّا تُرِيَنِّي}: the majority read «تُرِيَنِّي» with a plain yāʾ. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk [read] «تُرِئَنِّي» with hamza in place of the yāʾ, like his reading «فإمَّا تَرَئِنَّ» and «لَتَرَؤُنَّ» with hamza; it is an irregular substitution.

semin-durr:94-94.t: His saying: {فَلاَ تَجْعَلْنِي}: the apodosis of the condition. And «رَبِّ» is a vocative, a parenthetical placed between the protasis and its consequence.

semin-durr:95-95.t: His saying: {على أَن نُّرِيَكَ}: attached to «لَقادِرون», or to an omitted element, according to a disagreement that has preceded, over whether this lām prevents what follows it from operating on what precedes it.

semin-durr:97-97.t: His saying: {مِنْ هَمَزَاتِ}: plural of «هَمْزَة», which is a prod and a thrust with the hand or otherwise. «والمِهْماز» (the spur) is a «مِفْعال» from that, like «المِحْراث» (the plough) from «الحَرْث». «والهَمَّاز» is one who finds fault with people, as if he thrusts with his tongue and prods with it.

semin-durr:99-99.t:
His saying: {حتى إِذَا}: there are several views on this «حتى». The first: that it is a limit for His saying «بما يَصِفون». The second: that it is a limit for «كاذبون». Al-Zamakhsharī's statement makes these two views clear: "«حتى» is attached to «يَصِفون», i.e. they continue in evil speech up to this time, the verse separating the two as a parenthetical and an emphasis." Then he said: "Or to His saying «وإنهم لكاذِبون»." I say: his saying "or to His saying such-and-such" is speech carried on the meaning, since the implied form is that «حتى» is suspended from «يَصِفُون» or from His saying «لَكاذِبون». In sum, it is a difficult expression.
The third: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«حتى» in these places is a particle of commencement. It may also be a pure limit, by implying omitted speech. The first is clearer, because what follows it is what is meant and intended to be mentioned." The Shaykh said: "Ibn ʿAṭiyya imagined that when «حتى» is a particle of commencement it cannot be a limit; but even if it is a particle of commencement, the sense of limit does not leave it; and he did not make clear the omitted, implied speech." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«حتى» is a limit with the sense of conjunction." The Shaykh said: "What appears to me is that there is an omitted clause before it, of which «حتى» is the limit, indicated by what precedes it. The implied form: «فلا أكونُ كالكفارِ الذين تَهْمِزُهم الشياطينُ ويَحْضُرونهم، حتى إذا جاء» ('so I shall not be like the disbelievers whom the devils prod and who are attended by them, until, when ... comes'). A parallel to its omission is the poet's saying:
3424 - فيا عَجَبا حتى كُلَيْبٌ تَسُبُّني ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
("What a wonder! Even Kulayb reviles me ...")
i.e. "all people revile me, even Kulayb"; except that in the verse what follows «حتى» indicates it, unlike the noble verse."
His saying: {رَبِّ ارجعون}: concerning His saying «ارْجِعُون» in the plural address there are three views, the best of which is that it is for glorification, as in the poet's saying:
3425 - فإنْ شِئْتِ حَرَّمْتُ النساءَ سِواكمُ ... وإن شِئْتِ لم أَطْعَمْ نُقاخاً ولا بَرْدا
("If you wish, I shall forbid myself women other than you [pl.]; and if you wish, I shall not taste cold sweet water nor sleep.")
And another said:
2326 - ألا فارْحَمُوني يا إلَهَ محمدٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
("Have mercy on me [pl.], O God of Muḥammad ...")
[Translator's note: this verse number is printed as 2326 in the source; 3426 would follow the sequence.]
From this verse may be taken something that refutes Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn ibn Mālik where he said: "I do not know anyone who permitted the supplicant to say: 'O Merciful ones'," saying: "so as not to suggest the opposite of tawḥīd." Yet the Exalted has reported of Himself with this form and its like, for glorification, in more than one place in His noble Book.
The second: that he called on his Lord and then addressed his Lord's angels with his saying «ارْجِعُون». On this view it is possible that there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «يا ملائكةَ ربي» ("O angels of my Lord"); then the muḍāf was omitted and he shifted to it by the return of the pronoun, as in His saying {وَكَم مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا} and then {أَوْ هُمْ قَآئِلُونَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 4], a shift towards the omitted «أهل» ("people").
The third: that this indicates repetition of the act, as if he had said «ارْجِعُون ارْجِعون ارْجِعون». Abū l-Baqāʾ reported it. It resembles what they said about His saying {أَلْقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ} [Qāf: 24], that it means «أَلْقِ أَلْقِ», the verb being put in the dual to indicate that; and they recited the saying:
3427 - قِفا نَبْكِ مِنْ ذِكْرى حبيبٍ ومَنْزِلِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
("Halt, you two, let us weep at the memory of a beloved and an abode ...")
i.e. «قِفْ قِفْ».

semin-durr:100-100.t:
His saying: {إِنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ}: it belongs to the category of using the part and intending the whole, as in the saying "The truest word a poet ever said is Labīd's word", meaning his saying:
3428 - ألا كلُّ شيءٍ ما خلا اللهَ باطِلُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
("Is not everything other than Allah vain ...")
A portion of this has already been given in the fullest wording in [Sūrat] Āl ʿImrān. And «هو قائلُها» is an adjective of «كلمة».
His saying: {بَرْزَخٌ}: «البَرْزَخْ» is the barrier between two incompatible things. It is also said: the veil between two things preventing one from reaching the other, and it is of the same meaning as the first. Al-Rāghib said: "Its origin is «بَرْزَه» with hāʾ, which was Arabicised. In the Resurrection it is what lies between a person and the lofty stations. And the barzakh before the resurrection is the prevention between a person and the return that he wishes for."

semin-durr:101-101.t:
His saying: {فِي الصور}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the ṣād and sukūn on the wāw. Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan [read it] with fatḥa on the wāw, as a plural of «صورة». Abū Razīn [read it] with kasra on the ṣād and fatḥa on the wāw, which is irregular; this is the reverse of «لحى» with ḍamma on the lām, plural of «لِحْية» with kasra.
His saying: {فَلاَ أَنسَابَ}: «الأنسابُ» is the plural of «نَسَب», which is kinship through birth, and by it connection is also expressed; in origin it is a maṣdar. The poet said:
3429 - لا نَسَبَ اليومَ ولا خُلَّةً ... اتَّسَعَ الخَرْقُ على الرَّاقِع
("There is no kinship today and no close friendship; the tear has grown too wide for the patcher.")
His saying: {بَيْنَهُمْ}: it may be attached to «أنساب» itself, and likewise «يومئذٍ», i.e. "there is no kinship between them on that day". It may also be attached to an omitted element, as an adjective of «أَنْساب». The tanwīn in «يومئذٍ» is a substitute for a clause, its implied form being «يومَ إذ يُنْفخ في الصُّور» ("the day when the Trumpet is blown").

semin-durr:103-103.t:
His saying: {فِي جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدُونَ}: «خالِدون» may be a second khabar of «أولئك», or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هم خالدون». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «في جهنم خالدون» is a badal from «خَسِروا أنفسَهم», and neither the substitute nor the thing substituted for has a position, because the ṣila has no position. The Shaykh said: "He made «في جهنم» a substitute for «خَسِروا», and this is a strange substitute. In reality the substitute would be the verb to which «في جهنم» is attached, i.e. 'they settled in Hell', and it is a badal of a thing for a thing, because whoever has lost himself settles in Hell."
I say: the Shaykh made the preposition and its genitive noun the substitute without «خالدون», while al-Zamakhsharī made all of that a substitute, as shown by his saying after that: "or a khabar after a khabar for «أولئك», or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ". These two suit only «خالدون»; as for «في جهنم», it is attached to it. So al-Zamakhsharī's statement needs an answer. Also «خالدون» would be left stranded. Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted the relative to be an adjective of the demonstrative noun, and there is something to consider in that, since the apparent view is that it is its khabar.

semin-durr:104-104.t:
His saying: {تَلْفَحُ}: it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl, or another khabar of «أولئك». «واللَّفحُ» is the fire's striking a thing, scorching and burning it, and it is stronger than «النَّفْخ». «النفخ» was already given in [Sūrat] al-Anbiyāʾ.
His saying: {كَالِحُونَ}: «الكُلُوح» is the drawing up of the upper lip and the slackening of the lower. In al-Tirmidhī: "his upper lip draws up until it reaches the middle of his head, and the lower slackens until it reaches his navel." From it comes «كُلوحُ الأَسَدِ», i.e. its baring its fangs. And «دهرٌ كالِحٌ» and «بردٌ كالحٌ», i.e. severe. It is also said: «الكُلُوْح» is frowning and grimness of the face. One says «كَلَح الرجلُ يَكْلَحُ كُلُوحاً وكِلاحاً».

semin-durr:106-106.t:
His saying: {شِقْوَتُنَا}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «شَقاوتُنا» with fatḥa on the shīn and an alif after the qāf. The rest [read it] with kasra on the shīn and sukūn on the qāf. They are two maṣdars of one meaning: «الشَّقاوة» is like «القَساوة», a widespread dialect, and «الشِّقْوةُ» is like «الفِطْنَة» and «النِّعْمة». Al-Farrāʾ recited:
3430 - كُلِّفَ مِنْ عَنائِهِ وشِقْوَتِهْ ... بنتَ ثمانِيَْ عَشْرةٍ مِنْ حِجَّتِهْ
("He was burdened, from his toil and his wretchedness, with a girl of eighteen years.")
It is the dialect of the Hijaz. Qatāda and al-Ḥasan, in one transmission, read like the two brothers except that they put kasra on the shīn. Shibl in his choice [read] like the rest, except that he put fatḥa on the shīn.

semin-durr:109-109.t: His saying: {إِنَّهُ كَانَ}: the majority read the hamza with kasra, as resumption. Ubayy and al-ʿAtakī [read it] with fatḥa, i.e. «لأنه» ("because it"). The hāʾ is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).

semin-durr:110-110.t:
His saying: {سِخْرِيَّاً}: the second object of «الاتخاذ». The two brothers and Nāfiʿ read it here and in [Sūrat] Ṣād with kasra on the sīn; the rest [read it] with ḍamma in [Sūrat] al-Muʾminūn. People disagreed about their meaning. It is said that they are of one meaning; this is the statement of al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Zayd. Yūnus said: "If service and forced labour (sukhra) is meant, then ḍamma and nothing else; if mockery is meant, then both ḍamma and kasra." Abū ʿAlī preferred the reading with kasra, and Makkī followed him; they said: because what follows suits it better, in His saying {وَكُنْتُمْ مِّنْهُمْ تَضْحَكُونَ}. I say: there is no proof in that, because they combined the two things: they pressed them into service in work, and they mocked them in ridicule. «والسُّخْرَة» with tāʾ is putting to service, and «سُخْرِيَّاً» with ḍamma comes from it, while «السُّخْرُ» without it is mockery, and the kasra form is from it. Al-Aʿshā said:
3431 - إنِّي أتاني حديثٌ لا أُسَرُّ به ... مِنْ عَلْوَ لا كَذِبٌ فيه ولا سُخْرُ
("News has come to me that does not please me, from on high, with no lie in it and no mockery.")
The Seven did not differ over the ḍamma in [Sūrat] al-Zukhruf, because service is meant there, and that supports the view of those who distinguish between them. However, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ibn Muslim and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh also put kasra there, and that supports the view of those who made them of one meaning.
The yāʾ in «سِخريَّاً» and «سُخْريَّاً» is the yāʾ of relation (nisba), added to indicate strength of the act; so «السُّخْرِيُّ» is stronger than «السُّخْر», as is said «خصوص» and «خصوصيَّة» to indicate the strength of that. Al-Zamakhsharī stated this meaning.

semin-durr:111-111.t: His saying: {أَنَّهُمْ هُمُ الفآئزون}: the two brothers read the hamza with kasra, as resumption. The rest [read it] with fatḥa, and there are two views on it; the more apparent is that it is causal, which agrees with the first, since the resumption is also given as a reason by it. The second, and al-Zamakhsharī mentioned no other, is that it is a second object of «جَزَيْتُهم», i.e. "[I rewarded them] because they ...", i.e. with their triumph. On the first, the second object is omitted.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {قَدْ أَفْلَحَ}: the majority read «أَفْلَحَ» with fatḥa on the hamza and the ḥāʾ, as an active past verb. Warsh, on his rule, transfers the vowel of the hamza to the silent letter before it and drops it. From Ḥamza in pausal form there is a difference: it was transmitted from him like Warsh and like the group. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «As for one who throws the vowel of the hamza onto the dāl and drops it, his reason is that the hamza, after its vowel is dropped, is turned into an alif, and then dropped because of its sukūn and the sukūn of the dāl before it in the original. The vowel of the dāl is not counted because it is accidental.» There is something to consider in his words, in two respects. One: that the eloquent dialect in the transfer is to drop the hamza altogether, so they say al-mara and al-kama for al-mar'a and al-kam'a. The weak dialect is to keep it and turn it into the vowel-letter of what precedes it, so they say al-marāh and al-kamāh with a lengthening in place of the hamza, like rās and fās for those who lighten them. So his saying "it is turned into an alif" is adopting the weaker of the two dialects.
The second: even if it is granted that it was turned into an alif, we do not grant that its dropping is due to its sukūn and the sukūn of the dāl in the original; rather it is dropped for a silent letter that is actually present in the pronunciation, namely the fāʾ of «أفلح», and whenever an apparent cause is found the ruling is referred to it rather than to an implied cause.
Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read «أُفْلِحَ» in the passive, that is: "they entered into success (falāḥ)". It is possible that it is from transitive aflaḥa; one says aflaḥahu, that is, he brought him to success, so aflaḥa is used both intransitively and transitively. Ṭalḥa also read «أَفْلَحُ» with fatḥa on the hamza and the lām and ḍamma on the ḥāʾ. Its explanation is that the original is «أَفْلحوا المؤمنون», with the plural marker attached before the agent, as in the dialect "the fleas ate me" (akalūnī l-barāghīth), and what I mentioned earlier at His saying {ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ كَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 71] and {وَأَسَرُّواْ النجوى الذين ظَلَمُواْ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 3] applies to it. ʿĪsā said: «I heard Ṭalḥa reading it, and I said to him: Are you making a grammatical error? He said: Yes, as my companions made an error», meaning: I followed them in what I recited. If they erred, on the supposition of the impossible, then I am erring following them. This shows the great care of the ancients for transmission and its precision, contrary to those who declare the transmitters mistaken.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «It is a rejected reading.» I (al-Samīn) say: I do not know how they reject it when the like of it is established in the Quran by consensus, namely the two verses just mentioned. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «And from him, that is from Ṭalḥa, «أَفْلَحُ» with a ḍamma without a wāw, the ḍamma sufficing in place of it, as in the saying:
3401 - فلَوْ أنَّ الأَطِبَّا كانُ حَوْلي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(If only the physicians had been around me …)»
There is something to consider in this, in that the wāw is not kept in a case like this in connected speech lest two silent letters meet, so the omission here is unavoidable; so how can he say "sufficing in place of it"? As for his comparing it with the verse, it is not a match, because its omission in the verse is necessary, whereas in the poem it is a poetic licence. This wāw is not heard in connected speech, but appears in pause and in writing.
The transmitters of Ṭalḥa's reading disagreed: is a written form given to the wāw? In the book of Ibn Khālawayh it is written with a wāw after the ḥāʾ, and in «al-Lawāmiḥ»: «The wāw after the ḥāʾ was dropped because they meet in connected speech, and the writing on it was carried over from the connected form, as in {وَيَمْحُ الله الباطل} [al-Shūrā: 24].» I say: and of it also {سَنَدْعُ الزبانية} [al-ʿAlaq: 18], {صَالِ الجحيم} [al-Ṣāffāt: 163].
And «قد» here is for expectation (tawaqquʿ). Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Qad is the opposite of «lammā»; it affirms what is expected and «lammā» negates it. There is no doubt that the believers were expecting this good news, and it is to inform them of the certainty of success for them, so they were addressed with what indicates the certainty of what they were expecting.»
[Translator's note: the source has «وتَدْييرُها» in the first objection, which I have rendered as "turn it into the vowel-letter of what precedes it"; the second objection's «لأنَّ حَذْفَها من الآيةِ ضروريٌّ ومن البيتِ ضرورةٌ» is rendered as it stands.]

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {فِي صَلاَتِهِمْ خَاشِعُونَ}: the prepositional phrase is attached to what follows it, and was fronted for emphasis; it is made fitting by the fact that what it is attached to is a verse ending (fāṣila), and likewise for what follows it of its sisters. The prayer was annexed to them because they are the ones who benefit from it, and the One prayed to is independent of it; so it was annexed to them and not to Him.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {لِلزَّكَاةِ}: the lām is redundant on the object because it precedes its governor and because it (the governor) is a derived form. Zakāh is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and is also applied to the amount taken out of the properties. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is a noun shared between a substance and a meaning. The substance: the amount that the giver of zakāh takes out of the nisāb. The meaning: the act of the giver of zakāh, and that is what Allah intended, so He made the givers of zakāh doers of it, and nothing else is permissible in it, because there is no maṣdar but it is expressed by the verb, and its originator is called a doer. You say of the one who strikes: the doer of the striking, and of the killer the doer of the killing, and of the giver of zakāh the doer of the purification, and the whole speech is on this. The verification of this is that in all events you say: who is its doer? And you are told: Allah or some of the creatures. The zakāh that denotes the substance is not barred from having [doers] attached to it because it falls outside what the doer can take on, but because the creatures are not its doers. They have recited the verse of Umayya ibn Abī l-Ṣalt:
3402 - المُطْعِمُون الطعامَ في السَّنَة ال ... أزمةِ والفاعلون للزكواتِ
(Those who feed food in the year of hardship, and the doers of the zakāhs)
It is also possible that zakāh is meant as the substance and an omitted muḍāf is implied, namely the paying; and taking the verse in this sense is sounder because in it it is in the plural.» I (al-Samīn) say: what drove Abū l-Qāsim (al-Zamakhsharī) to this is that some claimed that zakāh here must be the maṣdar, because had he meant the substance he would have said "payers" (muʾaddūn) and not "doers" (fāʿilūn); so al-Zamakhsharī said: that is not barred because the doer cannot take it on, but because the creatures are not its doers. He made the zakāhs in Umayya's verse substances only because of its plural, since a maṣdar is not pluralized. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) disputed with him and said: «It may be a maṣdar and was pluralized only for the difference of its kinds.»
[Translator's note: the source's wording of the Shaykh's remark is incomplete («يجوز أَنْ مصدراً»); it is rendered as "it may be a maṣdar", which is clearly intended.]
His saying: {إِلاَّ على أَزْوَاجِهِمْ}: there are several views on it. One: that it is attached to «حافِظون» by inclusion of another sense, meaning "holding back" or "confining"; both are made transitive by «على». The Exalted said: {أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ} [al-Aḥzāb: 37]. The second: that «على» has the meaning of «مِنْ», that is: "except from their wives", so «على» is in the sense of «مِنْ», just as «مِنْ» came in the sense of «على» in His saying {وَنَصَرْنَاهُ مِنَ القوم} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 77]; al-Farrāʾ held this. The third: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī said: that is, "except as those having authority over their wives, or those in charge of them", from your saying: "So-and-so was over so-and-so, and then died and left her, and so-and-so succeeded over her". Its like is: "Ziyād was over Basra", that is, a governor over it. From it is their saying: «Three are under so-and-so, and from there the woman is called a bed (firāsh).» The fourth: that it is attached to an omitted word indicated by «غيرُ مَلومين». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «as though it were said: "They are blamed except over their wives", that is: they are blamed for every sexual contact except what has been permitted to them, for they are not blamed for that.» I say: he did not make it attached to «ملومين» for two reasons. One: that what comes after «إنَّ» does not govern what is before it. The second: that the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern what is before the muḍāf; and also for the corruption of the meaning.
The fifth: that it be made a complement of «حافظين». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «from your saying "protect for me the rein of my horse"», by including the meaning of negation, as their saying «nashadtuka bi-llāhi illā faʿalta» includes the meaning "I ask nothing of you except your doing"», meaning that its form is affirmative and its meaning negative.
The Shaykh said, after I (al-Samīn) mentioned this from al-Zamakhsharī: «These are strained views in which foreignness (ʿujma) is apparent.» I say: what foreignness is there in that? Although the Shaykh made it attached to «حافظون» in the way he mentioned, by inclusion of another sense. And that is not sound for him unless he commits himself to one of these views, namely the interpretation by negation as in «nashadtuka llāh», because it is an emptied exception (mufarragh), and that is only after a negation or what has its meaning.
The sixth: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «in the position of accusative by «حافِظُون» in meaning; because the meaning is: "they have guarded them from every private part except from the private parts of their wives".» I say: there are two things in it: one, including in «حافظون» the sense of "guarded", and the second, including in «على» the sense of «عن».
His saying: {أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ}: «ما» has the meaning of «اللاتي» ("those who", feminine). There are two views on its applying to rational beings. One: that it applies to kinds, as in {فانكحوا مَا طَابَ}, that is, "kinds". The second: al-Zamakhsharī said: «what is meant is, from the genus of rational beings, those that run like non-rational ones, and they are the females.» The Shaykh said: «His saying "wa-hum" is not good, because the word "hum" is specific to males; he should have said "wa-huwa" on the form of «ما», or "wa-hunna" on its sense.» I say: the answer is that the pronoun refers back to rational beings, so his saying "wa-hum" means: "and the rational beings are the females".

semin-durr:112-112.t:
His saying: {قَالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ}: the two brothers read «قل: كم لَبِثْتُمْ» and «قُلْ إنْ لبثتم» with the imperative in both places; Ibn Kathīr, like the two brothers, in the first only; and the rest «قال» in both places, as a report about Allah or the angel. The two verbs are written without an alif in the Kufan codices, and with an alif in the codices of Mecca, Medina, Syria and Basra. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī agreed with the Kufan codices, while ʿĀṣim differed from them, or agreed with them on the assumption that the alif was omitted from the script but intended. Ibn Kathīr agreed in the second with the Meccan codices, and in the first with others, or came to them on the assumption that the alif was omitted but intended. As for the rest, they agreed with their own codices in the first and the second.
«كم» is in the accusative position as an adverbial of time, i.e. "how many years". And «عددَ» is a badal from «كم»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. Others said: «عدد سنين» is a tamyīz of «كم», and this is the sound view.
Al-Aʿmash and al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿĀṣim read «عَدَداً» with tanwīn. There are several views on it. The first: that «عدداً» is a maṣdar put in the place of the noun, so it is an adjective placed before what it describes; the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said this. He means that the original is «سنين عدداً», i.e. "counted" [years], but the adjective is obligatorily placed before the described; so the correct thing would be for him to say: it is accusative as a ḥāl. This is the school of the Basrans. The second: that «لَبِثْتُم» means «عَدَدْتُم» ("you counted"), so the accusative of «عدداً» is as a maṣdar, and «سنين» is a badal from it. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» also said: "There is remoteness in it, because staying does not indicate counting." The third: that «عدداً» is a tamyīz of «كم» and «سنين» is a badal from it.

semin-durr:113-113.t: His saying: {العآدين}: plural of «عادٍّ», from «العَدَد» (number). Al-Ḥasan and al-Kisāʾī in one transmission read it with the dāl lightened, the plural of «عادٍ», active participle of «عدا», i.e. the wrongdoers. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It has been read lightened in the sense of the earlier peoples, like your saying «وهذه بِئْرٌ عادية» ('this is an ancient well'), i.e. ask those who came before us. One of the two yāʾs of the nisba was dropped, as they said «الأشعرون», and the other was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters." I say: what is dropped first is the second yāʾ, because it is the vowelled one, and by dropping it two quiescent letters meet. What Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned is supported by what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned, who said: "«العادِيِّين» has also been read, i.e. the ancients, the long-lived, for they regard it [the sojourn] as short, so how much more those lesser than they?" Ibn Khālawayh said: "And there is another dialect, «العاديِّين»," meaning with a doubled yāʾ, plural of «عادِيَّة» in the sense of the ancients.

semin-durr:114-114.t: His saying: {لَّوْ أَنَّكُمْ}: its apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "if you knew the measure of your stay, in its length, you would not have answered with this duration." «قليلاً» is accusative as an adjective of an omitted noun of time or an omitted maṣdar, i.e. «إلاَّ زمناً قليلاً» or «إلاَّ لُبْثاً قليلاً» ("except a short time" / "except a short stay").

semin-durr:115-115.t:
His saying: {عَبَثاً}: there are two views on its accusative. The first: that it is a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. «عابثين» ("in jest"). The second: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. "for the sake of futility". «العَبَثُ» is play and what has no benefit, and anything that has no sound purpose. One says «عَبَثَ يَعْبَثُ عَبَثاً» when he mixes his work with play. Its origin is from their saying «عَبَثْتُ الأَقِطَ», i.e. "I mixed the dried cheese". «والعَبِيْثُ» is food mixed with something, and from it comes «العَوْبَثَانِيُّ», for dates, barley-meal and clarified butter mixed together.
His saying: {وَأَنَّكُمْ}: it may be conjoined to {أَنَّمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ}, so the thinking extends over it; and it may be conjoined to «عبثاً» if that is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be conjoined to «عبثاً», i.e. for futility and for your being left not returned." He put «إلينا» before «تُرْجَعون» for the sake of the verse-endings.
His saying: {لاَ تُرْجَعُونَ}: this is the khabar of «أنَّكم». The two brothers read «تَرْجِعُون» in the active; the rest in the passive. It has already been said that «رَجَعَ» may be intransitive and transitive. It is also said that it is only transitive and the object is omitted.

semin-durr:116-116.t: His saying: {الكريم}: the majority read it in the genitive as an adjective of «العرش»; it is so described because good things descend from it, or because it is ascribed to the Most Generous of the generous. Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ismāʿīl from Ibn Kathīr, and Abān ibn Taghlib read it in the nominative. There are two views on it. The first: that it is also an adjective of «العرش», but cut off from its case for the sake of praise, as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. This is good, because the two readings agree in meaning. The second: that it is an adjective of «رب».

semin-durr:117-117.t:
His saying: {وَمَن يَدْعُ}: a condition. There are two views about its apodosis; the sounder is that it is His saying «فإنما حِسابُه». On this, concerning the preceding clause, His saying {لاَ بُرْهَانَ لَهُ بِهِ}, there are two views. The first: that it is an adjective of «إلهاً», and it is an inseparable adjective, i.e. the god invoked besides Allah can only be so; hence it has no implied contrary meaning (mafhūm), because the meaning would be spoiled. Similar is {وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ} [al-Anʿām: 38]: it is not understood that there is another god invoked besides Allah who has proof, or that there is a bird that flies without its two wings. The second: that it is a parenthetical clause between the condition and its apodosis. Al-Zamakhsharī pointed to the two views with his saying: "It is an inseparable adjective, like «يَطير بجناحيه»; it is brought for emphasis, not that among the gods there is any for whom proof could be established. And it may be a parenthetical between the condition and the consequence, as you say: 'Whoever does good to Zayd — and none is more deserving of kindness than he — Allah will reward him'."
The second of the first two views: that the apodosis of the condition is "His saying «لا بُرْهانَ له به»", as if he fled from the implied contrary meaning of the adjective because of the spoiling it entails, and so fell into something not permitted except in poetic necessity, namely omitting the fāʾ of the consequence from a nominal clause, as in the verse:
3432 - مَنْ يَفْعَلِ الحسناتِ اللهُ يَشْكُرُها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
("Whoever does good deeds, Allah thanks him for them ...")
[to the end of] the verse. The explanation of «لا برهانَ له» as an adjective has already been given. There is no difficulty, because it is an inseparable adjective, or because it is a parenthetical clause.
His saying: {إِنَّهُ لاَ يُفْلِحُ}: the majority read the hamza with kasra, as a resumption that conveys knowledge. Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda [read] «أنه» with fatḥa. Al-Zamakhsharī explained it as the khabar of «حِسابُه»; he said: "its meaning: his reckoning is the non-success. The original: his reckoning is that he does not prosper; so «الكافرون» was put in place of the pronoun, because «مَنْ يَدْعُ» has the meaning of a plural, and likewise «حِسابُه أنه لا يُفلح» is in the sense 'their reckoning is that they do not prosper'." End of quotation. It may also be on the omission of the causal particle, i.e. [«ل»]«أنَّه لا يُفْلح». Al-Ḥasan read «لا يَفْلح» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and lām, imperfect of «فَلَح» in the sense of «أفلح»; faʿala and afʿala have one meaning in it. And Allah knows best; He speaks the truth and guides to the way.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {لأَمَانَاتِهِمْ}: Ibn Kathīr read «لأماناتِهم» in the singular here and in «Saʾala» (al-Maʿārij); the rest read it in the plural. In meaning they are the same, since generality is intended, and the plural is more fitting. Amāna is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) and is applied to the thing entrusted, as in His saying {أَن تُؤدُّواْ الأمانات إلى أَهْلِهَا} [al-Nisāʾ: 58] and {وتخونوا أَمَانَاتِكُمْ} [al-Anfāl: 27], and it is substances, not meanings, that are returned and betrayed; so said al-Zamakhsharī. As for what he mentioned from the two verses, it is conceded. As for this noble verse, it admits the maṣdar and admits the substance.
Al-Akhawān read «على صلاتِهم» in the singular; the rest read «صَلَواتهم» in the plural. There is no disagreement in al-Maʿārij, and the singular and plural are as given earlier for «أمانتهم» and «أماناتهم». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: how did He repeat the mention of prayer at the beginning and at the end? I say: they are two different mentions and not a repetition; they were first described as humble in their prayer and finally as guarding it.» Then he said: «Also, it was in the singular first to convey humility in the genus of prayer, whichever prayer it may be, and in the plural at the end to convey guarding its numbers, namely the five prayers, the witr and the regular sunnas.»
I (al-Samīn) say: this is directed only at the reading of other than the two (al-Akhawān). As for al-Akhawān, they put it in the singular at the beginning and at the end. Although al-Zamakhsharī himself narrated the disagreement over the plural and singular of the second prayer with respect to the reading.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ}: this sentence may be resumptive, and may be an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), either from the agent of «يَرِثُون» or from its object, since the mention of each of them is in it.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {مِن سُلاَلَةٍ}: there are two views on it. One, which is the apparent, is that it is attached to «خَلَقْنا», and «مِنْ» is of beginning of the extent. The second: that it is attached to an omitted word, as a ḥāl from «الإنسان». Sulāla is of the pattern fuʿāla, a pattern that indicates smallness, like qulāma (nail-clipping). It is from salaltu l-shayʾa mina l-shayʾ, that is, you drew it out of it; from it their saying "he is the sulāla of his father", as though he were drawn out of his loins. It was recited:
3403 - فجاءت به عَضْبَ الأَديمِ غَضَنْفَراً ... سُلالةَ فَرْجٍ كان غيرَ حَصِيْنِ
(She brought him forth, sharp-skinned, a lion, the extract of a private part that was not guarded)
and Umayya ibn Abī l-Ṣalt said:
3404 - خَلَقَ البَرِيَّةَ مِنْ سُلالةِ مُنْتِنٍ ... وإلى السُّلالَةِ كلِّها سَنعودُ
(He created creation from a foul extract, and to the extract, all of it, we shall return)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Sulāla is the pure essence, because it is drawn out from among the impurity.» This sentence is the answer to an omitted oath, that is: "By Allah, We have indeed created". It was conjoined to the sentence before it because of the fitting relation between them, which is that when He, the Exalted, mentioned that those characterized by those qualities will inherit al-Firdaws, which implies mention of the return in the Hereafter, He mentioned the first creation so as to argue from it for the return, since the beginning is by custom harder than the repetition, as in His saying {وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ} [al-Rūm: 27]. This is better than the statement of Ibn ʿAṭiyya: «This is the beginning of a speech, and the wāw at its start conjoins a sentence of speech to a sentence of speech, even if they differ in meaning», because I have given you the aspect of the fitting relation.
His saying: {مِّن طِينٍ}: there are two views on «مِنْ». One: that it is of beginning of the extent. The second: that it is to explain the genus. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: what is the difference between «min» and «min»? I say: the first is for beginning and the second for explanation, as in His saying {مِنَ الأوثان}.» The Shaykh said: «It cannot be explanatory unless we say that sulāla is itself the clay. But if we say that it is what is drawn out of clay, then «min» is of beginning of the extent.»
As for what this «مِنْ» is attached to, there are several views. One: that it is attached to an omitted word, as it is an adjective of «سُلالة». The second: that it is attached to «سُلالة» itself, because it has the meaning of "drawn out" (maslūla). The third: that it is attached to «خَلَقْنا» because it is a badal from the first, if we say that sulāla is the clay itself.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاهُ نُطْفَةً}: there are two views on this pronoun. One: that it refers to the human being (al-insān). If anyone other than Ādam is meant, it is clear, and his creation from an extract of clay is the creation of his origin, who is Ādam, so it is on the omission of a muḍāf. If Ādam is meant by it, then the pronoun refers to his offspring, that is, "We made his offspring", so it is also on the omission of a muḍāf. Or the pronoun refers to the human being to whom that is fitting, who is the offspring of Ādam; the word al-insān, as such, is suitable for the origin and the branch, and each thing returns to what is fitting for it. Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this.
His saying: {فِي قَرَارٍ}: it may be attached to the "making" (jaʿl), and may be attached to an omitted word as an adjective of «نُطْفَة». Qarār is the place of settling, which is the location of abiding. What is meant by it is the womb. It was described as «مَكِيْن» (firm) for the firmness (makāna) which is a quality of what settles in it, for one of two senses: either figuratively, like "a travelling road", when it is the one in it who travels; or for its firmness in itself, because it has become firm where it is and is well guarded.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا النطفة عَلَقَةً} and what follows it: «خَلَق» includes the sense of "making" (jaʿala) in the sense of transformation, so it is transitive to two objects, just as jaʿala includes the sense of khalaqa and so is transitive to one, as in {وَجَعَلَ الظلمات والنور} [al-Anʿām: 1].
His saying: {عِظَاماً}: the majority read «عِظاماً» and «العظام» in the plural in both. Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «عَظْماً» and «العظم» in the singular in both. Al-Sulamī, al-Aʿraj and al-Aʿmash read the first in the singular and the second in the plural. Abū Rajāʾ, Mujāhid and Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Bakr read the first in the plural and the second in the singular, the reverse of the previous. The plural is on the original, because it corresponds to what is meant, and the singular is for the genus, as in His saying {وَهَنَ العظم مِنِّي} [Maryam: 4]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «He put the singular in the place of the plural because the confusion is removed, since the human being has many bones.» The Shaykh said: «According to Sībawayh and his companions this is not permissible except out of necessity, and they recited:
3405 - كُلوا في بَعْضِ بطنِكُم تَعِفُّوا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Eat in part of your belly, you will be chaste …)
even though it is known that each one has a belly.» I say: and like it:
3406 - لا تُنْكِروا القَتْلَ وقد سُبِيْنا ... في حَلْقِكم عَظْمٌ وقد شُجينا
(Do not deny the killing, for we have been taken captive; in your throats is a bone, and we have been choked)
he means: "in your throats". And like it the saying of another:
3407 - به جِيَفُ الحَسْرى فأمَّا عِظامُها ... فبِيْضٌ وأمَّا جِلْدُها فصَلِيْبُ
(In it are the carcasses of worn-out camels; as for their bones, they are white, and as for their hide, it is hard)
he means: "their hides". And of it is {وعلى سَمْعِهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 7]; a part of this has already been given.
His saying: {أَحْسَنَ الخالقين}: there are three views on it. One: that it is a badal (substitute) for the Majestic Name. The second: that it is an adjective (naʿt) of the Majestic Name, and it is preferable to the previous, because a badal with a derived word is rare. The third: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "He is the best". The default is that there is no implication. Abū l-Baqāʾ forbade that it be a description, saying: «because it is indefinite even if annexed to a definite, because the muḍāf ilayhi is a replacement for «من», and so are all forms of afʿal followed by "than you".» I say: he built this on one of two views about the elative afʿal when it is annexed: is its annexation genuine (maḥḍa) or not? The sound one is the first.
And «الخالقين», that is, "those who measure out", as in the saying of Zuhayr:
3408 - ولأنتَ تَفْرِيْ ما خَلَقْتَ وبَعْ ... ضُ القومِ يَخْلُقُ ثم لا يَفْرِي
(You cut what you have measured out, while some of the people measure out and then do not cut)
The specification (mumayyiz) of afʿal is omitted because the muḍāf ilayhi indicates it, that is: "the best of the creators in creation", that is, "of those who measure out, in measuring", like His saying {أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَاتَلُونَ} [al-Ḥajj: 39], that is: "to fight"; what permission was given for is omitted because the ṣila indicates it.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {بَعْدَ ذلك}: that is, after what has been mentioned, and for that reason the demonstrative is singular. The majority read «لَمَيِّتُون». Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «لَمائِتون». The difference between them is that mayyit indicates permanence and settledness, and māʾit indicates occurrence, like ḍayyiq and ḍāʾiq, and farih and fārih. So of one who will die one says mayyit and māʾit, and of one who has died, mayyit only and not māʾit, because the quality is settled and permanent; the like of it will come in al-Zumar, if Allah the Exalted wills. If it is asked: no two people differ over death, while how many differ over the resurrection, so why did He strengthen what is agreed upon with the strongest emphasis and omit that degree of emphasis for what is disputed? The answer: because the evidences for the resurrection are abundant and mutually supporting, it was brought out in the form of what is agreed upon and needs no such emphasis; and because they did not work for death and did not care about its affairs, they were placed in the position of one who denies it, so He brought them out in the form of the denier who thinks it utterly improbable.
The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) was asked about that. He answered that the lām mostly makes the imperfect purely present, and it cannot enter «تُبْعثون» because that is made purely future by its governing a future adverbial. He objected to himself with His saying {وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ القيامة} [al-Naḥl: 124], for the lām entered the imperfect which governs a future adverbial, namely the Day of Resurrection. He answered that this is excluded by his word "mostly", or that the governor of «يوم القيامة» is implied. There is something to consider in this which is not hidden, since in it the governor is prepared to govern and then cut off from it.
And «بعد ذلك» is attached to «مَيِّتون», and the lām of inceptive (lām al-ibtidāʾ) does not prevent that.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {على ذَهَابٍ بِهِ}: «على ذَهابٍ» is attached to «لَقادرون», and the lām, as already stated, does not prevent that; and «به» is attached to «ذَهاب», and the bāʾ is equivalent to the hamza (of transitivization), like it in {لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 20], that is, "to cause it to go away".

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {وَشَجَرَةً}: conjoined to «جناتٍ». Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «سِيناء» with kasra on the sīn; the rest read it with fatḥa. Al-Aʿmash likewise, except that he shortened it. As for the first reading, the hamza in it is not for the feminine, since in the language there is no fiʿlāʾ with kasra on the first whose hamza is feminine; rather it is for attachment (ilḥāq), like «sirdāḥ» and «qirṭās», so it is like «ʿilbāʾ», and the hamza is converted from a yāʾ or wāw, because attachment is done with them; when the weak letter occurred at the end after an extra alif it was converted to a hamza, like ridāʾ and kisāʾ. Al-Fārisī said: «It is the yāʾ that appeared in "dirḥāya".» The dirḥāya is the short, fat man.
Abū l-Baqāʾ made this hamza radical (original), saying: «The hamza on this is a root, like "ḥimlāq", and is not feminine since in the language there is nothing like [ḥamrāʾ, and the yāʾ is a root, since in the language there is no "sanaʾ"]», meaning the root sīn-nūn-hamza. This contradicts what was said earlier, that it is substituted for an extra letter attached to the root.
